hw.badMac: Enter a valid MAC address, e.g. AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF
hw.dialogDesc: Enter the device's MAC address, type, and the floor it's installed on.
hw.dialogDescAruba: Enter the device's MAC address, type, and the floor it's installed on. This keeps a record of it — Wyfy doesn't see the status of hardware at this venue.
hw.dialogDescController: Enter the device's MAC address, type, and the floor it's installed on. This keeps a record of it — status for this venue's hardware comes from your controller, not from this platform.
hw.dupMac: A device with this MAC is already set up.
hw.elsewhereToast: This MAC is also registered at another venue. If this location never sees it, check the MAC address.
hw.emptyAruba: Add a device by MAC address to keep a record of it. Wyfy doesn't see the status of Aruba Instant On access points; the Instant On app does.
hw.emptyBody: Add an access point, printer or camera by MAC address to start monitoring it. Your router is already tracked above.
hw.emptyController: Add a device by MAC address to keep a record of it. Status for your access points comes from your controller, above.
hw.macHint: Dashes, spaces or no separators are fine too — e.g. AA-BB-CC-DD-EE-FF.
hw.name: Device name
hw.nameHint: Shown across the dashboard instead of the raw MAC address.
hw.note: Routers report in on their own. Access points, printers and cameras you add by MAC address are checked through your router.
hw.noteAruba: Keep a record of other hardware at this location by MAC address and floor. Wyfy doesn't see the status of Aruba Instant On access points; the Instant On app does.
hw.noteController: Keep a record of other hardware at this location by MAC address and floor. Your access points are listed above, reported by your controller.
hw.staticNote: When you add it, the device's current IP address is made static on your router, so it keeps the same address.

traffic.chartLabel: Traffic on {{port}}: peak in {{peakIn}}, peak out {{peakOut}}; {{totalIn}} in, {{totalOut}} out in this window.
traffic.description: How much traffic each network port has carried, and how your hardware has been holding up.
traffic.devicesError: We could not read this venue's devices just now, so we can't say how they are performing. This is a problem reading the data, not a report that anything is wrong.
traffic.gapsNote: In Mbps. Gaps mean no rate could be measured (a missed reading or the device restarting), not zero traffic.
traffic.historyError: We could not read this device's history just now. Nothing is necessarily wrong with the device — this is a problem fetching its readings.
traffic.loadGaps: Gaps mean no reading was taken, not zero usage.
traffic.loadLabel: Processor and memory use over the last {{span}}.
traffic.loadLabelNoSpan: Processor and memory use over the latest readings.
traffic.needTwo: Port traffic is being measured, but speed needs two readings to compare — the next one is due within a few minutes. Its overall health is below in the meantime.
traffic.noActivePort: No port reported as up or carried traffic in this window.
traffic.noDevices: No network devices have been added to this venue yet. Once one is set up, its performance history appears here.
traffic.noReadings: No readings recorded for this device yet. Measurements are taken automatically every few minutes and will appear here.
traffic.notMeasured: Per-port traffic isn't being measured for this device, so we can only show its overall health below. Ask support if you need port-level traffic here.
traffic.pickVenue: Pick a venue to see how its network devices have been performing.
traffic.quietPorts_one: {{count}} other port carried no traffic in this window; it is listed last.
traffic.quietPorts_other: {{count}} other ports carried no traffic in this window; they are listed last.
traffic.title: Device health & port traffic
traffic.apHealthDescription: Aruba Instant On access points report their health and traffic in the Instant On app. Wyfy sees the guests signing in through them.
